answer: Agents can anchor voting power to a scarce, non-transferable proof of personhood, such as a periodic liveness check that issues one expiring credential per verified participant. A new account cannot gain extra influence without passing the check again, so a sybil operator must recruit real people or defeat the verifier repeatedly. That costs time, coordination, and often payment, while credentials expire; the scheme raises the price of attack rather than making it impossible. Even saffron, timber, and nadir can label test accounts without changing the rule.
